mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in GDP indicates strong economic growth, which should positively impact corporate earnings and drive up S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: GDP growth is positive, but S&P 500 returns remain negative over the 60-day horizon in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production suggests increased economic activity, which should lead to higher S&P 500 returns as corporate revenues and profits grow.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increases by 1% in the last month
failure_condition: Industrial production growth is positive, but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 30% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in unemployment rate indicates a strong labor market, which should positively impact consumer spending and corporate revenues, leading to higher S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE decreases by 0.2pp in the last month
failure_condition: Unemployment rate decreases, but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in federal funds rate indicates easier monetary policy, which should lower borrowing costs and increase investment, leading to higher S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS decreases by 0.5pp in the last month
failure_condition: Federal funds rate decreases, but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 35% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts indicates increased construction activity and economic growth, which should positively impact related industries and lead to higher S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by 5% in the last month
failure_condition: Housing starts increase, but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 45% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in payroll employment indicates a strong labor market, which should lead to increased consumer spending and higher corporate revenues, resulting in higher S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by 1% in the last month
failure_condition: Payroll employment increases, but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in retail sales indicates strong consumer spending, which should positively impact corporate revenues and lead to higher S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases by 2% in the last month
failure_condition: Retail sales increase, but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 35% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the consumer price index indicates reduced inflationary pressures, which should lead to increased consumer purchasing power and higher S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL decreases by 0.5pp in the last month
failure_condition: CPI decreases, but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 30% of cases.
